text: dsh-auto-upgrade 是用于维护 DSH profile 的插件，通过 skills 注册器提供扫描与人工执行技能，并部署 PowerShell 脚本。它可检查已安装依赖和版本兼容性，在隔离 profile 验证候选版本，预览并切换升级，也可回滚恢复。适合希望分阶段更新 DSH 插件的用户。需要 Windows 与 PowerShell 7；候选安装需要 pnpm，在线查询 npm 最新标签时需要网络。

dsh-auto-upgrade maintains DSH profiles with scan and user-triggered apply skills. It checks dependency compatibility, verifies candidates in isolation, switches after preview, and supports rollback. Requires Windows, PowerShell 7, and pnpm; optional npm tag checks need network.
想检查 DSH profile 里的插件有哪些可更新、是否兼容。
升级插件前，能不能先在隔离环境验证再决定是否切换？
I need to roll back a DSH profile after an update causes trouble.
dsh-auto-upgrade 的功能「扫描兼容性」：扫描所选 profile 的依赖、检查版本兼容并生成报告与快照；启用 Online 时还查询 npm 标签。通过扫描脚本触发。
dsh-auto-upgrade 的功能「验证与切换」：在隔离 profile 验证候选版本，通过后可预览并确认切换；需要时用恢复脚本回滚。
dsh-auto-upgrade 仅在扫描启用 Online 时向 registry.npmjs.org 请求包的 dist-tags，以比较最新版本；默认扫描不执行该查询。

**Version:** `0.1.1-rc.2` (tested on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Requirements](docs/REQUIREMENTS.html) · [Plan](docs/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md)

A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) bundle that scans your installed profiles for updates, stages
the update in an isolated home, gates it, and then switches by two directory renames —
with a rollback that needs no network and no reinstall.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · dsh-auto-upgrade：> **Work in progress.** This is `0.1.x`: the read-only scan, the candidate pipeline and
> the reversible switch work today; the parts that make it fully unattended (functional
> probe matrix, dual-end orchestration, scheduled self-upgrade) are planned but **not
> implemented yet**. The table below is the honest state, not the aspiration.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · What works today：| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Read-only scan: per-profile dependency inventory, source classification (npm / file / link / git), engine + peer gate, snapshot, report, root entry file | ✅ |
| Candidate build in an isolated home (own `node_modules`), dump gate, isolated boot gate | ✅ |
| Switch (two renames), rollback (reverse rename), commit; recovery-intent record before the first rename | ✅ |
| Executor deployment: `scripts/` copied to `$DSH_HOME/auto-upgrade/scripts/` on mount | ✅ |
| Functional probe matrix (tool-level A/B diff against the live profile) | ⏳ planned (M2) |
| Dual-end orchestration: verify on Web first, then prepare Desktop | ⏳ planned (M3) |
| Self-update chain + scheduled duty session (automation task) | ⏳ planned (M4) |
| Installing a plugin that is not installed yet; natural-language config | ⏳ planned (M5) |

dsh-auto-upgrade README · What works today：Tested end to end on Web with two real upgrades (`clearai-dsh` 0.5.5 → 0.5.6 and
`@changfenhuang/dsh-genui` 0.13.0 → 0.14.0, one at a time), each followed by a host
restart and a health check. The Desktop side is not covered yet.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · Requirements：- Windows 10/11 with PowerShell 7.
- A DSH install whose profile you want to maintain (developed and tested against
  `0.2.1-rc.2`; `engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`).
- `pnpm` on `PATH` — the candidate build installs into an isolated profile.
- Network (or a warm pnpm store) when the target version is not cached.

The switch does **not** stop the host for you: a running DSH keeps its files open, so
stop it first (on this machine: stop `dsh web`, run
`$DSH_HOME\DSH-Hidden-Launcher.vbs` afterwards). A failure inside the switch compensates
back to the previous state; nothing is ever deleted.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · How it is put together：| Layer | What it does | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| **Bundle** | one `insert` row, a ~110-line skill registrar | ships, enables and disables like any plugin, and can be removed completely |
| **Skill** | judging: compatibility, safety, overlap, local forks; a user-only apply gate | knowledge that has to be rewritten every release |
| **Scripts** | scan, snapshot, gates, promote, roll back | deterministic, offline, zero tokens |

dsh-auto-upgrade README · How it is put together：The registrar imports **nothing** from `@deepseek-ai/*`; the skills registry is reached
through `inject: ["skills"]` only. That is deliberate: a helper plugin must not be the
thing the version gate rejects on upgrade day.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · What the gates actually check：- `dsh --profile

--dump-default-config` — the bundle layer only, so a broken user patch layer cannot block it. Exit code plus `patch: entry … not found` warnings. - Every `engines.dsh` and every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer, resolved against the version the host actually ships. A peer that is not on disk is reported as *not resolvable* (client-side packages are bundled into the web client, so absence is not proof of removal) — it does not become a false failure. - An isolated boot on `--port 0`: parse the printed URL, probe it, treat `401` as alive (the Web surface authenticates by cookie), kill the whole process tree, time out. - A missing declaration is `unknown`, not a defect: recorded, never queued.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · Safety and degradation：- A scan changes nothing outside `$DSH_HOME/auto-upgrade/` (plus one entry file).
- The switch moves the live profile into `quarantine/<txn>/original` instead of deleting
  it, and writes a durable recovery-intent record before the first rename; a crash in
  between is replayable.
- Candidate and live must be on the same volume, so the swap stays atomic.
- The registrar deploys the executors outside the package, so a self-upgrade of the
  bundle cannot delete the thing doing the upgrading.
- No UI, ever: everything is configured by asking the agent in a session.

dsh-auto-upgrade README · Known limits：- `0.1.x` covers one plugin at a time; DSH-core upgrades and the Desktop half are not
  automated yet (M2/M3).
- Functional regression detection is composition-level today (gates + evidence); a
  tool-level A/B probe matrix is not implemented.
- Windows only. Candidate builds need `pnpm` and, unless the store is warm, network.
- Not published to npm yet: install from the tarball.
